verses.english: Linked Discourses 41.5
1. With Citta
With Kāmabhū (1st)

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā kāmabhū macchikāsaṇḍe viharati ambāṭakavane.
verses.english: At one time Venerable Kāmabhū was staying near Macchikāsaṇḍa in the Wild Mango Grove.

verses.pali: Atha kho citto gahapati yenāyasmā kāmabhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ kāmabhuṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho cittaṁ gahapatiṁ āyasmā kāmabhū etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Citta the householder went up to Venerable Kāmabhū, bowed, and sat down to one side. Kāmabhū said to him,
“Householder, there is this saying:
‘With faultless parts and white canopy,
the one-spoked chariot rolls on.
See it come, untroubled,
with stream cut, unbound.’

verses.pali: Imassa nu kho, gahapati, saṅkhittena bhāsitassa kathaṁ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti?
verses.english: How should we see the detailed meaning of this brief statement?”

verses.pali: “Kiṁ nu kho etaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā bhāsitan”ti?
verses.english: “Sir, was this spoken by the Buddha?”
“Yes, householder.”

verses.pali: “Tena hi, bhante, muhuttaṁ āgamehi yāvassa atthaṁ pekkhāmī”ti.
verses.english: “Well then, sir, please wait a while as I consider the meaning of this.”

verses.pali: Atha kho citto gahapati muhuttaṁ tuṇhī hutvā āyasmantaṁ kāmabhuṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then after staying silent for a while, Citta said to Kāmabhū:
“Sir, ‘faultless parts’ is a term for ethics.
‘White canopy’ is a term for freedom.
‘One spoke’ is a term for mindfulness.
‘Rolls on’ is a term for going forward and coming back.

verses.pali: ‘Ratho’ti kho, bhante, imassetaṁ cātumahābhūtikassa kāyassa adhivacanaṁ mātāpettikasambhavassa odanakummāsūpacayassa aniccucchādanaparimaddanabhedanaviddhaṁsanadhammassa.
verses.english: ‘Chariot’ is a term for this body made up of the four principal states, produced by mother and father, built up from rice and porridge, liable to impermanence, to wearing away and erosion, to breaking up and destruction.

verses.pali: Rāgo kho, bhante, nīgho, doso nīgho, moho nīgho.
verses.english: Greed, hate, and delusion are troubles.

verses.pali: Te khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
verses.english: A mendicant who has ended the defilements has given these up, cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, and obliterated them, so they are unable to arise in the future.
That’s why a mendicant who has ended the defilements is called ‘untroubled’.
‘The one who comes’ is a term for the perfected one.
‘Stream’ is a term for craving.

verses.pali: Sā khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
verses.english: A mendicant who has ended the defilements has given this up, cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, and obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.
That’s why a mendicant who has ended the defilements is said to have ‘cut the stream’.

verses.pali: Rāgo kho, bhante, bandhanaṁ, doso bandhanaṁ, moho bandhanaṁ.
verses.english: Greed, hate, and delusion are bonds.

verses.pali: Te khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
verses.english: A mendicant who has ended the defilements has given these up, cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, and obliterated them, so they are unable to arise in the future.
That’s why a mendicant who has ended the defilements is called ‘unbound’.

verses.pali: Iti kho, bhante, yaṁ taṁ bhagavatā vuttaṁ:
verses.english: So, sir, that’s how I understand the detailed meaning of what the Buddha said in brief:
‘With faultless parts and white canopy,
the one-spoked chariot rolls on.
See it come, untroubled,
with stream cut, unbound.’”

verses.pali: Imassa kho, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmī”ti.

verses.english: “You’re fortunate, householder, so very fortunate,

verses.pali: Yassa te gambhīre buddhavacane paññācakkhu kamatī”ti.
verses.english: to traverse the Buddha’s deep teachings with the eye of wisdom.”
